Definition: from G4171; to be (engaged) in warfare, i.e. to battle (literally or figuratively):--fight, (make) war.
BiblicalUsage: Polemeo means to war, to battle. The dragon and his angels fought in Revelation 12:7, and the Lamb shall overcome them that make war with Him in Revelation 17:14. James asks, From whence come wars and fightings among you, in James 4:2, and Jesus warns the church at Pergamos, I will fight against them with the sword of my mouth, in Revelation 2:16.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe there is a war I cannot see and a war I can — and both are won the same way, by the Lamb who overcomes. That is why I hold that my fightings start in my own lusts, and end at His feet.
